questions: Does the restored 0.09 m track bring oval progress back to about 0.87 with the current controller, or does the controller change alone move it? This separates geometry from controller effects.
Are s-bend and slalom max_error still at 0.061 to 0.063? If they are, the bend exit is not turn authority or sensing, and geometry should stop changing.
Does steering_oscillation on the oval stay near or below 0.3? If it rises, the next change is controller damping, not geometry.
Does line_loss_events stay at or below 1.0 per run on every track?

intent: Restore the iteration 3 best geometry exactly (five 16 mm sensors at x = ±0.04, ±0.02, 0 and y = 0.06; wheel_track 0.09 m; body 0.22 m long, 0.12 m wide; mass 0.5 kg; wheel radius 0.03 m). Iteration 6 showed that narrowing to 0.085 m drops oval progress below 0.85, so the track goes back to 0.09 m. The aim is a stable, known-good platform for the Integrator to retune, with bend-exit work moved to the controller.
learning: Narrowing wheel_track to 0.085 m (iteration 6) lowered oval progress from 0.87 to 0.70 and did not move the bend exits, so turn authority was not the limit at that width. Iterations 4 and 5 showed that outer spacing and 12 mm footprints also fail to fix the bends. Across all geometry tested, s-bend and slalom max_error sits at 0.061 to 0.064, so the remaining bend-exit gap appears to be controller- or speed-limited. The next geometry test, if the oval holds, is y = 0.07 with everything else at the best design, to check whether even earlier sensing lowers the bend-exit max_error without raising oscillation.
rationale: Iteration 6 narrowed wheel_track from 0.09 to 0.085 m on the iteration 3 geometry and scored 155.17, below the 203.20 best. Oval progress fell from 0.87 to 0.70 and oval steering_oscillation was 0.266. Oval max_error stayed at about 0.061, and s-bend (0.0629) and slalom (0.0610) did not move below the 0.06 off-track limit. The narrower track therefore over-steered and cost progress without fixing the bend exits. The Integrator's rule for this case applies: oval progress below 0.85 at 0.085 m means returning wheel_track to 0.09 m. The sensor row (y = 0.06, x = ±0.04, 16 mm footprints) stays, because iterations 4 and 5 showed that outer spacing and 12 mm footprints both cost progress. Iteration 7 therefore restores the iteration 3 geometry exactly, which is the best-scoring geometry tested (203.20). This gives the Integrator a stable platform, and any further change in score can be attributed to the controller. Across every geometry since iteration 2, s-bend and slalom max_error has stayed at 0.061 to 0.064, so the bend-exit limit is probably controller-side or speed-side, not geometry. The next geometry hypothesis, if the Integrator's controller holds the oval, is a forward row at y = 0.07, which I expect to help only if it lowers oval max_error without raising oscillation. Expected result: a score near 203, with oval progress at or above 0.85 and max_error near 0.06.
